dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.druid_openi: This is old wood, and I keep it. If one of yours dies for good, bring their body here before ten days are out. Lay it at my feet and the wood will lend them a new one.
Softly. The grove is listening. I stand here so the dead for good have somewhere to come back to: carry the body under these trees in time, and I'll ask the wood for another.
You've found my grove. I'm only its keeper. A body brought to me within ten days of a death for good gets up again, in whatever blood the wood chooses.
I've stood in these trees longer than the village down the way has had a name. The wood gives new bodies to the dead, if someone cares enough to carry the old one here.
The druid touches the nearest trunk, then the ground at their feet, and waits to see if you understand.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.druid_wants: And if your road takes you through other woods, bring me something my grove has never grown: %s.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.name_druid: Names are for people who move about. The wood calls me nothing. You can call me %s.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.druid.thanks.0: %s! It's been years since I held one. Let's give it a place.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.druid.thanks.1: You carried that all this way for an old hermit's grove? Thank you. It'll take root.
speech.jaymoskingdoms.druid.thanks.2: Oh, that's a good one. The wood will remember who brought it here.
